title: Global generation for sheaves supported on closed points
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed
field and $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$. Let $F$ be an
abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ whose support is contained in the set of
closed points of $X$. Then $F$ is
globally generated.
(*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F1F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1F), second
assertion.)

proof.text: By [lem-kun-cp-approximation], write $F=\varinjlim_{i\in I}F_i$ as a filtered colimit of finitely generated subsheaves, each supported on a finite set $Z_i$ of closed points. Give $Z_i$ its reduced closed subscheme structure and denote the inclusion by $j_i:Z_i\to X$. The last assertion of that node gives $F_i\cong j_{i*}(F_i|_{Z_i})$, in the sense of [lem-kun-04ca]; the latter's essential-image assertion applies to arbitrary abelian sheaves with these vanishing stalks outside $Z_i$. Put $G_i=F_i|_{Z_i}$ and fix an isomorphism $\alpha_i:F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{i*}G_i$. Fix $i$ for Steps 2--5. No finiteness or torsion hypothesis on the stalk groups of $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the global-generation assertion

proof.text: The finite space $Z_i$ is discrete: every singleton is closed by [def-weil-closed-points], and its complement is a finite union of closed singletons. Hence $Z_i$ is the disjoint union of its open singleton subschemes $Z_{i,z}$. Each $Z_{i,z}$ has an affine neighbourhood, necessarily all of $Z_{i,z}$, so write $Z_{i,z}=\operatorname{Spec}A_z$ using the scheme notion [def-pc-scheme]. Its ring $A_z$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and has a unique prime $\mathfrak p_z$, necessarily minimal and maximal. Every element outside $\mathfrak p_z$ is a unit, so $A_z=(A_z)_{\mathfrak p_z}$; [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] makes this a field. It is the residue field of $Z_i$ at $z$. This equals $\kappa_X(z)$: on an affine chart of $X$, the closed immersion is a quotient $R\to R/J$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and at the corresponding maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supset J$ its residue field is $(R/J)_{\mathfrak m/J}/(\mathfrak m/J)(R/J)_{\mathfrak m/J}=R_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak mR_{\mathfrak m}$, the field of [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus $Z_i=\coprod_{z\in Z_i}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_X(z)$. This also covers the empty set, with empty coproduct.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the global-generation assertion; the sentence that Z_i is a finite disjoint union of spectra of separably closed fields; algebra.tex Tag 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring) supplies the field calculation

proof.text: For each $z\in Z_i$, [lem-kun-closed-point-field](b) applies to the original finite-type $K$-scheme $X$ and its closed point $z$: $\kappa_X(z)$ is separably closed, even when it is a nontrivial purely inseparable extension of $K$. Let $H_z$ be the restriction of $G_i$ to $Z_{i,z}=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_X(z)$. By [lem-kun-03qu-global-generation], $H_z$ is globally generated. Its evaluation morphism of [def-kun-global-generated], with coefficients $\mathbf Z$, is therefore surjective on every geometric stalk by [lem-kun-global-generated-stalkwise]. More explicitly, the constant sheaf of [def-kun-constant-sheaf] has stalk $\mathbf Z$: given a locally constant integer-valued section on a pointed neighbourhood, take a covering on which it is constant and a member containing a lift of the geometric point. On this pointed refinement the section equals its integer value. Representatives with the same value therefore define the same germ, and every integer occurs as a constant section. By [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits], the stalk of its evaluation source is $\bigoplus_{s\in H_z(Z_{i,z})}\mathbf Z$. Consequently every $a\in(H_z)_{\bar z}$ has the form $a=\sum_{r=1}^m n_r(s_r)_{\bar z}$ with $n_r\in\mathbf Z$ and $s_r\in H_z(Z_{i,z})$. This uses global generation only; it does not assert that the sections-to-stalk map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the global-generation assertion

proof.text: Every section $s\in H_z(Z_{i,z})=G_i(Z_{i,z})$ extends to a section $t\in G_i(Z_i)$ by taking $s$ on $Z_{i,z}$ and zero on every other singleton component. These components are an etale covering: their inclusions are open immersions and hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and they are jointly surjective as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For two distinct components the intersection is empty, and on a component intersected with itself the two restrictions agree. Thus the matching-family equalizer in [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] gives the required section, uniquely. The same sheaf axiom for the empty cover says $G_i(\varnothing)=0$. By the underived direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $(j_{i*}G_i)(X)=G_i(X\times_XZ_i)=G_i(Z_i)$, so $t$ corresponds, through $\alpha_i(X)^{-1}$, to a global section $\widetilde t$ of $F_i$.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the global-generation assertion

proof.text: Check the evaluation morphism of $F_i$ from [def-kun-global-generated] at every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$. If its underlying point is outside $Z_i$, then $(F_i)_{\bar x}=0$: by [def-kun-support], being outside the support means that no geometric point over this underlying point has a nonzero stalk. Thus surjectivity holds without invoking independence of the geometric-point choice. If it lies over $z\in Z_i$, the geometric point factors through $Z_i$: in a quotient chart $R\to R/J$ from [def-weil-closed-immersion], the map $R\to\Omega$ has kernel containing $J$ since its point lies in $V(J)$. Write $\bar z$ for this factorization. The stalk map of $\alpha_i$ followed by [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] gives $(F_i)_{\bar x}\cong(G_i)_{\bar z}=(H_z)_{\bar z}$. For the last equality use the germ definition [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. A representative $(W,\bar w,u)$ on $Z_i$ restricts to $(W\times_{Z_i}Z_{i,z},\bar w,u|_{W\times_{Z_i}Z_{i,z}})$, a pointed refinement because $\bar w$ lies over $z$. In the other direction a representative on the open component is the same section on that neighbourhood viewed over $Z_i$. These maps are inverse on germs: one composite is the identity and the other is restriction along the displayed pointed refinement, which represents the same germ in the colimit. Under the closed-immersion stalk identification, the germ of the global section $\widetilde t$ of Step 4 is the germ of $s$; indeed the base-change functor in [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] sends the neighbourhood $(X,\bar x)$ to $(Z_i,\bar z)$ and the direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] sends the section to $t$; naturality of the sheaf isomorphism $\alpha_i$ with respect to restrictions gives the same section after taking germs. For an arbitrary target stalk element, take its finite expression $\sum_r n_r(s_r)_{\bar z}$ from Step 3 and extend each $s_r$ by Step 4. The element $\sum_r n_r1_{\widetilde t_r}$ in the evaluation source maps to it. Thus the evaluation is surjective on every geometric stalk; [lem-kun-global-generated-stalkwise] proves that $F_i$ is globally generated. If $Z_i=\varnothing$, all target stalks are zero and the same conclusion holds.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the global-generation assertion

proof.text: Steps 1--5 show that every member $F_i$ of the filtered presentation is globally generated. Its index can be taken small: in the universe used for the site, subsheaves of the fixed $F$ are compatible choices of subgroups $F_i(U)\subseteq F(U)$, hence form a subset of $\prod_U\mathcal P(F(U))$; the finitely generated ones form a subset of this set. Ordered by inclusion they are filtered by Step 1. Apply [lem-kun-colim-gbl-gen] to this small filtered diagram on the fixed site $X_{\Et}$. Its global-generation definition agrees with [def-kun-global-generated]: $X$ is the final object of $X_{\Et}$, so a compatible family of sections is determined by its value in $F_i(X)$. The sheaf colimit is $F$ by Step 1, so $F$ is globally generated, as required.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed
field and $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$. Let $F$ be an
abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ whose support is contained in the set of
closed points of $X$. Then $F$ is
globally generated.

proof.text:
As in the preceding proof, $X$ is Noetherian and
[lem-kun-cp-approximation] gives a presentation
$F=\varinjlim_iF_i$ by finitely generated subsheaves, the support of
$F_i$ being a finite set $Z_i$ of closed points of $X$; after
giving $Z_i$ its reduced structure, [lem-kun-04ca] writes
$F_i=i_*\mathcal G_i$ for the finite closed immersion
$i:Z_i\to X$.

We claim the evaluation map

$$
\operatorname{ev}_i:\bigoplus_{s\in H^0(X_{\Et},F_i)}
\underline{\mathbf Z}\longrightarrow F_i
$$

of [def-kun-global-generated] is surjective. A geometric stalk
away from $Z_i$ is zero. At a geometric point over
$z\in Z_i$, the finite-direct-image stalk formula
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] identifies the target with
the corresponding stalk of $\mathcal G_i$ on
$\Spec(\kappa(z))$. The residue field $\kappa(z)$ is a finite
purely inseparable extension of the separably closed field $K$,
hence is separably closed by
[lem-kun-closed-point-field]; therefore
[lem-kun-03qu-global-generation] identifies the sections over
the component $\Spec(\kappa(z))$ with that stalk. Since
$H^0(X_{\Et},F_i)=H^0((Z_i)_{\Et},\mathcal G_i)$ by
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] (and $\Gamma$ of a disjoint union
is the product of the global sections), every element of the target
stalk is the germ of a global section, so
$(\operatorname{ev}_i)_{\bar z}$ is surjective. Thus $F_i$ is
globally generated in the sense of
[lem-kun-global-generated-stalkwise]. Finally
[lem-kun-colim-gbl-gen] shows that the filtered colimit $F$ is
globally generated.
